summary.en: Syrian authorities arrested the suspect known as the "Butcher of Baniyas" for the 2013 coastal massacres and sentenced two individuals to death for the 2025 coastal sectarian violence. Two Syrian pipelines were damaged in attacks on energy infrastructure, and a gas export pipeline in northeastern Syria was hit, causing a fire. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu disclosed a direct conversation with President Ahmed al-Sharaa following a 2025 strike in Damascus. Syrian sources said the discussion involved U.S. and Arab mediation. The conflict produced 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Syriske myndigheter arresterte den mistenkte kjent som «Baniyas-slakteren» for massakrene langs kysten i 2013, og dømte to personer til døden for den sekteriske volden langs kysten i 2025. To syriske rørledninger ble skadet i angrep på energiinfrastruktur, og en gasseksportledning i nordøst-Syria ble truffet, noe som førte til brann. Israels statsminister Netanyahu opplyste om en direkte samtale med president Ahmed al-Sharaa etter et angrep i Damaskus i 2025. Syriske kilder sa at diskusjonen omhandlet amerikansk og arabisk mekling. Konflikten førte til 2 732 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
background.extract: Disputes and clashes in Syria have continued following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, which many sources consider the end of the Syrian civil war. Numerous actors are involved, including clashes between the newly-formed Syrian caretaker government and later the Syrian transitional government led by the former emir of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) and incumbent president Ahmed al-Sharaa, Assad loyalists, Alawite groups, and Druze insurgents; clashes between elements of the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army (SNA) and the government on one side, and formerly the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on the other; as well as an Israeli invasion and occupation of the demilitarized buffer zone in southwestern Syria.
